rule_timeline.label: Older regulatory baseline
rule_timeline.detail: Title 19, Sec. 19-13-D8t(m): 1.90 total nursing and aide hours and 0.64 licensed hours per patient day for chronic and convalescent nursing homes. The same subsection excludes director of nurses time in homes of 61+ beds and assistant director time in homes of 121+ beds from counting toward the minimums.

rule_timeline.label: Statute directs a 3-hour standard
rule_timeline.detail: Public Act 21-185 (CGS Sec. 19a-563h) directed DPH to set minimum staffing of three hours of direct care per resident per day by January 1, 2022. DPH said revised regulations would not be in place by that date.

rule_timeline.label: DPH 3.0 policies take effect
rule_timeline.detail: Former DPH policies: 0.84 hours of nursing care plus 2.16 hours of nurse aide services per resident per day (3.00 total).

rule_timeline.label: Amended DPH policies
rule_timeline.detail: 3.0 hours of total nursing and nurse aide care per resident per day, of which 0.84 hours provided by licensed nursing personnel.

legislation.title: An Act Concerning Nursing Home Staffing Ratios
legislation.summary: Proposed raising the minimum from 3.0 to 3.6 direct-care hours per resident per day and adding fines of up to $10,000 per violation.
legislation.status: Not enacted. Last action March 18, 2025: favorable report, tabled for the Senate calendar.

legislation.title: Nursing home bed moratorium exceptions, resident data, and related-party rate caps
legislation.summary: Aging Committee bill on Department of Social Services recommendations: bed moratorium exceptions, timely resident data for rate setting, and excluding related-party employees from rate cost determinations. Not a staffing-ratio bill.
legislation.status: Last action March 23, 2026: favorable report, tabled for the Senate calendar. The bill status page lists no public act.

legislation.title: Funding of the quality metrics program for nursing homes
legislation.summary: Aging Committee bill to implement the Department of Social Services quality metrics program for nursing homes. Not a staffing-ratio bill.
legislation.status: Last action April 14, 2026: favorable report, tabled for the Senate calendar after Appropriations. The bill status page lists no public act.

workforce_context.label: CNA wage pathway
workforce_context.detail: A May 2025 agreement between the State and SEIU 1199NE sets a pathway to $26 per hour for nursing home CNAs by January 1, 2028, funded through incremental Medicaid increases.

workforce_context.label: Temporary nursing services agencies
workforce_context.detail: Since January 1, 2023, temporary nursing services agencies must register with DPH and report itemized revenues and costs and average fees by type of nursing personnel. DPH does not publish this data online.

dss_case_mix.label: Connecticut Medicaid case mix index (CMI), statewide quarterly averages
dss_case_mix.note: Published by DSS for its acuity-based Medicaid reimbursement. Higher values mean a higher average resident acuity. This is a different measure from the CMS case-mix staffing comparison points used elsewhere in these tools. Transcribed from the DSS page; verify against the source on refresh.

legislation_note: Bills listed are those found in searches through October 30, 2026. A bill's content can also pass inside a budget or implementer act, so check the Connecticut General Assembly site before relying on this list.
